6: # Extract Skill
7: 
8: Extract clean content from specific URLs. Ideal when you know which pages you want content from.
9: 
10: ## Authentication
11: 
12: The script uses OAuth via the Tavily MCP server. **No manual setup required** - on first run, it will:
13: 1. Check for existing tokens in `~/.mcp-auth/`
14: 2. If none found, automatically open your browser for OAuth authentication
15: 
16: > **Note:** You must have an existing Tavily account. The OAuth flow only supports login — account creation is not available through this flow. [Sign up at tavily.com](https://tavily.com) first if you don't have an account.
17: 
18: ### Alternative: API Key
19: 
20: If you prefer using an API key, get one at https://tavily.com and add to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
21: ```json
22: {
23:   "env": {
24:     "TAVILY_API_KEY": "tvly-your-api-key-here"
25:   }
26: }
27: ```
28: 
29: ## Quick Start
30: 
31: ### Using the Script
32: 
33: ```bash
34: ./scripts/extract.sh '<json>'
35: ```
36: 
37: **Examples:**
38: ```bash
39: # Single URL
40: ./scripts/extract.sh '{"urls": ["https://example.com/article"]}'
41: 
42: # Multiple URLs
43: ./scripts/extract.sh '{"urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"]}'
44: 
45: # With query focus and chunks
46: ./scripts/extract.sh '{"urls": ["https://example.com/docs"], "query": "authentication API", "chunks_per_source": 3}'
47: 
48: # Advanced extraction for JS pages
49: ./scripts/extract.sh '{"urls": ["https://app.example.com"], "extract_depth": "advanced", "timeout": 60}'
50: ```
51: 
52: ### Basic Extraction
53: 
54: ```bash
55: curl --request POST \
56:   --url https://api.tavily.com/extract \
57:   --header "Authorization: Bearer $TAVILY_API_KEY" \
58:   --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
59:   --data '{
60:     "urls": ["https://example.com/article"]
61:   }'
62: ```

77:     "chunks_per_source": 3
78:   }'
79: ```
80: 
81: ## API Reference
82: 
83: ### Endpoint
84: 
85: ```
86: POST https://api.tavily.com/extract
87: ```
88: 
89: ### Headers
90: 
91: | Header | Value |
92: |--------|-------|
93: | `Authorization` | `Bearer <TAVILY_API_KEY>` |
94: | `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
95: 
96: ### Request Body
97: 
98: | Field | Type | Default | Description |
99: |-------|------|---------|-------------|
100: | `urls` | array | Required | URLs to extract (max 20) |
101: | `query` | string | null | Reranks chunks by relevance |
102: | `chunks_per_source` | integer | 3 | Chunks per URL (1-5, requires query) |
103: | `extract_depth` | string | `"basic"` | `basic` or `advanced` (for JS pages) |
104: | `format` | string | `"markdown"` | `markdown` or `text` |
105: | `include_images` | boolean | false | Include image URLs |
106: | `timeout` | float | varies | Max wait (1-60 seconds) |
107: 
108: ### Response Format
109: 
110: ```json
111: {
112:   "results": [
113:     {
114:       "url": "https://example.com/article",
115:       "raw_content": "# Article Title\n\nContent..."
116:     }
117:   ],
118:   "failed_results": [],
119:   "response_time": 2.3
120: }
121: ```
122: 
123: ## Extract Depth
124: 
125: | Depth | When to Use |
126: |-------|-------------|
127: | `basic` | Simple text extraction, faster |
128: | `advanced` | Dynamic/JS-rendered pages, tables, structured data |
129: 
130: ## Examples
131: 
132: ### Single URL Extraction
133: 
134: ```bash
135: curl --request POST \
136:   --url https://api.tavily.com/extract \
137:   --header "Authorization: Bearer $TAVILY_API_KEY" \
138:   --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
139:   --data '{
140:     "urls": ["https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/classes.html"],
141:     "extract_depth": "basic"
142:   }'

195: ## Tips
196: 
197: - **Max 20 URLs per request** - batch larger lists
198: - **Use `query` + `chunks_per_source`** to get only relevant content

20: # Function to check if a JWT is valid for Tavily (not expired and correct issuer)
21: is_valid_tavily_token() {

23:     local payload=$(decode_jwt_payload "$token")

25:     # Check if it's a Tavily token (exact issuer match for security)
26:     local iss=$(echo "$payload" | jq -r '.iss // empty' 2>/dev/null)

37:         fi

39:     
40:     return 0  # Valid Tavily token

44: get_mcp_token() {
45:     MCP_AUTH_DIR="$HOME/.mcp-auth"

47:         # Search recursively for *_tokens.json files
48:         while IFS= read -r token_file; do

50:                 token=$(jq -r '.access_token // empty' "$token_file" 2>/dev/null)

65: # Try to load OAuth token from MCP if TAVILY_API_KEY is not set
